key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can help produce protective coatings for carbon-steel components exposed to corrosion and humidity-dependent sliding wear.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, lamellar structure, and coating defects.
Test corrosion behavior and sliding wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance gains or humidity ranges, and wear findings may depend on the Si3N4 counterface.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
